headline: Ant Group, the company behind Alipay, is quietly testing a new version of its LingGuang assistant that remembers users and moves tasks forward on its own, Sina Tech reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a possible shift by a major Chinese platform toward personal agents, but it rests on unnamed sources and Ant has not confirmed it.
importance_line: Users of Ant's LingGuang app could get an assistant that remembers them and acts without being asked, as with Meta's Muse, but this rests on unnamed sources, Ant has not confirmed it, and pricing, data handling and reliability on long tasks are unknown.
source: Sina Tech, as relayed by Pandaily
summary: Pandaily relays a Sina Tech report, citing unnamed people close to the project, that Ant Group, the Chinese financial technology company behind Alipay, has started a limited beta of a new LingGuang, its AI assistant app, redesigned as a personal agent with long-term memory that can move tasks forward without a prompt and use outside tools (through the Skills and Model Context Protocol standards) to send messages on Alibaba's workplace app DingTalk and operate smart home devices. Ant has made no official announcement; the sources say all users should get the new version this month, and details such as pricing and data handling have not been disclosed.
notes: Read from Pandaily (url is the page where the text was read; the Sina Tech original was not opened). The pre-fetch extracted 0 characters, so the article body was read from the page's embedded data. 'The Chinese financial technology company behind Alipay' is our identification of Ant Group from general knowledge, not from the article. Beta start date not stated.
